scope: Label likelihood in observed absence, linked to P26 calibration and depth-conditioned identity gates.

source_observations.finding: foreign marks another positive physical ID; a background label is excluded as a missing detection.
foreign_on_surface collapses all other positive identities into a single count conditional on matching depth and no contemporaneous own identity.
label histories are learned only under identified_in_place and sufficient on-surface support. They estimate selected in-place disagreement, not absent/replacement emissions.
The current code fits label pseudo-moments but forces ok_lab=false. Removing this forces an uncalibrated absent-uniform law used by the geometric channel onto a different conditional observation.

identifiability_argument.observation: Let T be the saved on-surface foreign fraction, G the common depth/association selection, and E the identified-in-place training event.
identifiability_argument.available: At most a robust summary of P(T|H_S,G,E); neither full P(T|H_S,G) nor P(T|H_A,G) is identified by these summaries.
identifiability_argument.counterexample: Hold the selected stationary emission fixed. Both P(T|H_A,G)=P(T|H_S,G) and a different normalized replacement emission are compatible with the same saved stationary statistics. The first has label LR=1; the second may support either hypothesis. No stationary-summary-only rule identifies which LR to apply.
identifiability_argument.selection_and_dependence: The E and G conditions are generated using the same depth/identity samples; multiplying independently fitted geo/label factors can count that selection twice.
identifiability_argument.prior_boundary: The persistence q supplies prior state odds. It cannot supply an unidentified label confusion likelihood.

real_requirement: Missing/foreign segmentation labels must not delete a still-present object; actual same-site replacement must remain expressible when there is identified evidence.
permitted_next_step: Recover existing sufficient conditional confusion information if supplied by existing runtime inputs; otherwise retain neutral label factor. Do not tune a label confidence from real or synthetic GT, do not invent an absent-uniform label distribution.
